title: fix(mobile): usePullToRefresh arms on a host that mounts after the first render (objectui#10105)
body:
Fixes #10105

Clause-②: no

Implemented by the `domain:ui` seat #1 dev run, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01BA3nKVUwKQJf8DBxrSVtNC`. Generic type parameters are written in words below (for example "`useRef` of T"), because GitHub strips angle-bracket fragments from PR bodies.

## What was wrong

`usePullToRefresh` (`@object-ui/mobile`) returns an object ref, so the hook never learns when a consumer attaches it. It bound its native `touchstart` / `touchmove` / `touchend` listeners in an effect keyed only on its three handlers and `enabled`, and that effect read `ref.current` exactly once.

On `ObjectCalendar`'s internal-fetch path the first commit is the loading screen. That screen carries no ref, so the one read found `null`. When the rows arrived the host mounted, but none of the effect's keys had changed, so the effect never ran again. The pull gesture did nothing, with no error, warning or hint. With pre-fetched `data` the first commit already contains the host, so the same gesture worked. That is the asymmetry the card reports.

## The repair (producer-side, in the hook)

The binding now follows the element, not the mount:

- A binding effect with no dependency list runs after every commit. It re-binds only when the element the listeners should be on (`ref.current`, or null while disabled) differs from the element they are on. This compares DOM identity, never memoised identity (AGENTS.md §5 #10).
- The native listeners are stable for the life of a binding and call the latest handlers through a ref. A state change, such as each `pullDistance` step during a gesture, no longer re-binds anything.
- A separate unmount effect releases the last binding. It removes exactly the listener functions that were added, which are recorded on the binding.

⛔ The exported signature and return type are unchanged. The declaration emitted for `usePullToRefresh.ts` at BASE `62597c58` and at HEAD is byte-identical: the same isolated `tsc --declaration --emitDeclarationOnly` over the file gives md5 `dc757400f43d65d92b5816029a7e100f` for both, and `cmp` exits 0. The returned `ref` is still the object ref (`RefObject` of T or null) that consumers pass to `ref=`. `ObjectCalendar.tsx` and the three sibling consumers are not edited.

## Both arms, one run, file state verified in the same command

The pin is `packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.pullToRefresh-10105.test.tsx`. It drives the hook's own native touch sequence on the host (touchstart at y=10, touchmove to y=110, then touchend), not a scripted scroll.

| hook file on disk | internal-fetch arm | pre-fetched arm (lit control) |
|---|---|---|
| blob `7b6a0926` (= HEAD blob = BASE blob, zero diff), first measurement before any edit | ✗ fails at the first pull: no indicator | ✓ |
| BASE blob `7b6a0926` (ablation mutation leg, at HEAD `875c9001`) | ✗ | ✓ |
| blob `5da0d858` (the fix; restore leg, blob == HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty) | ✓ | ✓ |

On the internal-fetch arm the pin also checks that a release past the threshold refetches (`find` 1 → 2). The second `find` is held open, so the test sees the loading screen with no calendar region. After the rows return, a second pull arms again and refetches (`find` 3).

## Which sibling consumers shared the defect (measured, not read)

A one-shot probe, not committed, drove the same gesture on each consumer's host on its internal-fetch path. Effects were flushed first, and the readings were written to a file. It ran in both ablation legs:

| consumer | hook at BASE | hook fixed |
|---|---|---|
| `ObjectGrid` | dead: no indicator, `find` stays 1 | arms, refetches (`find` 1 → 2) |
| `ObjectTimeline` | dead: no indicator, `find` stays 1 | arms, refetches (`find` 1 → 2) |
| `ListView` | arms, refetches | arms, refetches |

`ObjectGrid` and `ObjectTimeline` render a loading screen before their host, like the calendar. `ListView` renders its host on the first commit and was never affected. Their test suites were re-run (below); their sources were not edited.

## Product-visible changes: read this before flipping ready

- **Nothing changes in what renders during loading.** No loading screen, skeleton or host was moved. Acceptance item 3's condition does not trigger. This line exists so that is said, not assumed.
- **The pull gesture now works where it was dead:** the internal-fetch paths of `ObjectCalendar`, `ObjectGrid` and `ObjectTimeline`.
- **Nested pull hosts now have one owner, the OUTERMOST armed pull host.** A pull on a view inside `ListView` bubbles to `ListView`'s host. An inner host lets the gesture go when an armed pull host is its DOM ancestor. Indicators per pull inside `ListView` (calendar / grid / timeline): BASE 2/1/2, round-1 head `875c9001` 2/2/2, head `8155fe27` **1/1/1**, with one refetch each throughout. While bound, armed hosts carry a `data-pull-to-refresh-host` attribute (not exported, not a documented contract). This follows the seat's decision on objectui#10105 (comment `5809834105`).

## Ablation (one-shot; no permanent mutation test left behind)

The fix was committed first. The mutation is the whole hook file reverted to its BASE content. It was verified on disk by blob hash (== BASE blob `7b6a0926`), `bindPullListeners` count 0, and the old dependency-list line count 1. The restore was `git checkout HEAD -- ABS_PATH` behind an EXIT/INT/TERM trap, and was verified by blob == HEAD blob `5da0d858` with `git diff HEAD` empty. `packages/mobile/dist` existed during the final run, but the root vitest config aliases `@object-ui/mobile` to `src`, and the mutation leg going red with a fixed `dist` present shows that `src` is what was measured.

At HEAD `875c9001`:
- Mutation leg: 3 red and 5 green.
  - Red: the calendar internal-fetch arm, the hook pin's late-host case, and its replaced-host case.
  - Green: the calendar pre-fetched arm, and the hook pin's control, StrictMode, unmount and `enabled` cases.
- Restore leg: 8/8 green.

Two more one-shot mutations went through `ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit, blob moved, restore proven). They show the StrictMode case can fail:
- M1: the unmount cleanup leaves the binding record set. The StrictMode case goes red because the binding is stranded.
- M2: the unmount cleanup does not unbind. The StrictMode case goes red because `onRefresh` is called 2 times, and the unmount case goes red too.

**Owner ablation at `8155fe27`.** `ablation-replace.mjs` WRAP removed `if (armedPullHostAbove(el)) return;` (1 → 0 hits; hook blob `104543d2` → `6aff16e7`). Mutation leg: 5 red (the 3 console nested pins and the 2 hook nested cases, all "got 2" indicators) and 11 green (the standalone grid and timeline, both calendar arms, and the late-attach, replace, StrictMode, unmount and enabled cases). Restore: blob == HEAD `104543d2`, `git diff HEAD` empty; 16/16 green.

## Tests and gates (final head `8155fe27`, tree clean)

- All from the repo root through the shared verify lock. `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=3 packages/mobile/ packages/plugin-calendar/ packages/plugin-timeline/ apps/console/src/__tests__/pullToRefreshOwner-10105.test.tsx`: 76/76 files, 685/685 tests, exit 0
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=3 packages/plugin-grid/`: 146/146 files, 1386/1386 tests, exit 0
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=3 packages/plugin-list/`: 82/82 files, 1005/1005 tests, exit 0
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/mobile type-check`, `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-calendar type-check` and `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console type-check`: each exit 0. They ran after `turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/console^...` (34/34 tasks). The console type-check is owed because it compiles the new consumer pin.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes` exit 0; `pnpm check:new-line-citations` exit 0 (0 new citations, merge base `62597c58`, 7 files compared); `pnpm check:phantom-deps` exit 0
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` exit 0; `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` exit 0; `pnpm check:changeset-claims` exit 0
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the 7 changed paths: NOT GOVERNED
- `eslint --format json` over the 7 changed files: 0 errors, and 0 warnings in new or changed code. The two `.md` files are config-ignored; the 7 warnings are in the pre-existing parts of the 10031 test. There is no type-aware linting, so this diff cannot move an untouched file's verdict. The repo-wide `pnpm lint`, and the full app-shell and console suites, are left to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- `ObjectCalendar.localizedSurface-10031.test.tsx`: only its comment changed. It described the dead internal-fetch path as a live defect and now points at the new pin.
- `useGesture` in the same package binds in the same kind of mount effect over an object ref. It has zero in-repo consumers (dormant), so it is not filed and not touched here. Carrier: none.
- On the pre-fetched path, `ObjectCalendar`'s own refresh bumps a key its fetch ignores. Inside `ListView` the gesture is now `ListView`'s alone, so that inert refresh no longer runs there. A pre-fetched calendar with no pull-hosting parent was not measured; this is an observation, not filed.
- Ownership is decided at touchstart and yields to any ARMED ancestor, whether or not that ancestor then engages (for example its own `isRefreshing`, or its `scrollTop`). `ListView`'s host is overflow-hidden, so it engages; other nestings were not measured.
- The consumer pin lives in `apps/console`, the one package that declares `ListView` plus all three child plugins (objectui#4409 dependency direction). It sits outside the claim's named surface, and the seat accepted it on review.
- Changeset: `.changeset/10105-pull-to-refresh-late-host.md`, a patch for `@object-ui/mobile`. The package README gains one paragraph saying the ref may attach late or be replaced.
